lines.trans: Do you have any debt with private loan sharks?
None at all.
Or were you ever active on any shady websites in the past?
Never, and I do not use social media either.
Then there is no problem—keep this cut in, and keep Cindy's expression too.
Um, Senior, could you please edit me out?
You do not want to? We are trying to make the show funny and you do not want to?
A 2 Days & 1 Night producer has to give up everything—having your unwashed face broadcast nationwide and all.
Baek Seung-chan has an innocent, sunny side, so viewers might really warm up to him.
Some staffers greedily chase screen time out of vanity, except viewers spot that like ghosts and instantly find them unlikable.

examples.trans: Do you have any debt with private loan sharks?

Here the word for 'debt' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예전 생각이 나서 그래, 예전에 선생님들 계실 때 생각해 봐.
examples.trans: It just reminds me of the old days—think back to when the veteran actresses were here.
Here the word for 'old days, past' is key.

meanings.note: Describes something unusual or out of the ordinary.
Used when sensing something is wrong.

examples.trans: The computer sounds a bit strange.
It's suspicious that he's suddenly being so nice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예전에 이상한 사이트에서 활동을 한 적이 있다거나?
examples.trans: Or were you ever active on any shady websites in the past?
Here the word for 'on websites' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예전에 이상한 사이트에서 활동을 한 적이 있다거나?
examples.trans: Or were you ever active on any shady websites in the past?
Here the word for 'activity' is key.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.

examples.text: 너 에스엔에스는 하니? 술은 자주 마실 거니?
examples.trans: Do you use social media? Are you going to drink often?
The topic of social media (SNS) came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!
Did you hear about this problem?
I was busy today because of problem.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그럼 문제 없네, 이거 살려, 신디 표정도 살리고.
examples.trans: Then there is no problem—keep this cut in, and keep Cindy's expression too.
This expression comes from 'keep it in'.

examples.text: 너 혜주 좋아하지? 하늘이 무너지는 표정을 짓더라.
examples.trans: You like Hye-joo, right? You looked like the sky was falling earlier.

examples.text: 까나리카노를 마시고 뿜는 표정이 웃겨야 되거든.
examples.trans: Her expression spitting out the fish-sauce coffee has to be hilarious.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 근데 선배님, 저는 좀 빼주시면 안 될까요?
examples.trans: Um, Senior, could you please edit me out?
This expression comes from 'if you take me out'.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Descriptive verb (adjective); the thing disliked takes the subject marker 이/가.

examples.trans: I really dislike rainy days.
You hate waking up early in the morning, right?

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.en: to be fun, to be entertaining
meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 재미있다.

examples.trans: This movie is really fun.
Studying Korean is fun.
I want to making right now.
How about trying to making together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this 1 night?
I was busy today because of 1 night.
Did you hear about this 2 days?
I was busy today because of 2 days.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 인간한테 가장 필요한 세 가지가 의식주인데, 편집실에 들어가면 의랑 주는 포기해야 된단 말이에요.
examples.trans: The three essentials for humans are clothing, food, and shelter, and once you enter the editing room you give up clothing and shelter.
This expression comes from 'must give up'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 1박 2일 PD는 다 포기해야 돼요, 세수도 못 했는데 얼굴 나가고 그런 거.
examples.trans: A 2 Days & 1 Night producer has to give up everything—having your unwashed face broadcast nationwide and all.
Here the word for 'even washing one's face' is key.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.
Did you hear about this face, though?
I was busy today because of face, though.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.

meanings.note: Determiner modifying a following noun.

examples.text: 그런 실수는 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake like that.
This is the first time I'm hearing a story like that.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 백승찬은 해맑은 데가 있어서 호감일 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Baek Seung-chan has an innocent, sunny side, so viewers might really warm up to him.
This expression comes from 'bright and innocent'.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 백승찬은 해맑은 데가 있어서 호감일 수 있어요.
examples.trans: Baek Seung-chan has an innocent, sunny side, so viewers might really warm up to him.
Here the word for 'likable' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 사심으로 방송 출연을 욕심내는 사람들도 있지만 시청자들은 귀신같이 알거든, 그럼 바로 비호감으로 찍히는 거지.
examples.trans: Some staffers greedily chase screen time out of vanity, except viewers spot that like ghosts and instantly find them unlikable.
Here the word for 'out of personal vanity' is key.

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.
Did you hear about this appearing on the show?
I was busy today because of appearing on the show.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 사심으로 방송 출연을 욕심내는 사람들도 있지만 시청자들은 귀신같이 알거든, 그럼 바로 비호감으로 찍히는 거지.
examples.trans: Some staffers greedily chase screen time out of vanity, except viewers spot that like ghosts and instantly find them unlikable.
This expression comes from 'coveting, being greedy for'.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Combines 시청 ('watching and listening') + 자 ('person').

examples.trans: Many viewers like that drama.
We listened carefully to viewer feedback.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 사심으로 방송 출연을 욕심내는 사람들도 있지만 시청자들은 귀신같이 알거든, 그럼 바로 비호감으로 찍히는 거지.
examples.trans: Some staffers greedily chase screen time out of vanity, except viewers spot that like ghosts and instantly find them unlikable.
Here the word for 'like ghosts, uncannily' is key.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

examples.trans: I'll start right away now.
The cafe is right in front of the school.
Did you hear about this as disliked?
I was busy today because of as disliked.

meanings.en: to get nicked, dented, or chipped
meanings.note: Passive form of 찍다 ('to strike/poke/stamp').
Used in 사진이 찍히다.

examples.trans: The car got a tiny nick.
The photo came out well.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
